title: Contribution hygiene: RFC scaffold, onboarding checklist, and deprecation signal registry for tokens+components
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Problem statement:
Redwood's component library has grown organically: tokens, buttons, tables, and charts see frequent small contributions but unclear entry/exit criteria. This causes inconsistent patterns, higher maintenance, and surprise regressions during rollouts. We need a practical, low-friction contributor hygiene workflow that: 1) standardizes the RFC intake/scaffold for design proposals; 2) provides a lightweight onboarding checklist for contributors (design, eng) tied to component types; and 3) formalizes a deprecation signal registry and phased sunset approach for UI tokens and components.

Scope:
- Applies to visual tokens, core interactive components (buttons, inputs), data surfaces (tables, charts), and layout primitives.
- Does NOT cover platform infra (auth, billing) or third-party integrations.

Outcomes we want:
- Faster, higher-quality contributions with fewer rework cycles.
- Predictable deprecation flows with automated signals and migration helpers.
- A reusable RFC scaffold that reduces back-and-forth and surfaces cost/compatibility tradeoffs early.

What this ticket delivers:
- RFC scaffold doc template with predefined sections (motivation, compatibility matrix, migration plan, perf implications, QA matrix).
- Contributor hygiene checklist differentiated by artifact type (tokens, interactive components, data surfaces).
- Deprecation Signal Registry: list of signals (telemetry thresholds, support requests, usage counts, perf regressions) and an automated tagging convention in the repo/issue tracker.
- A short rollout playbook for maintainers describing gated steps (canary, opt-out tokens, adapt layer).
- Links to example artifacts: Confluence proposal, a sample GitHub PR, and a mock migration codemod.

Non-goals:
- Rewriting the design system. This is a governance and workflow layer only.

References and artifacts:
- Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/DS/pages/Contrib+Hygiene+Playbook (draft)
- Design mocks (Drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1-example-mocks
- Example PR (frontend): https://github.com/redwood-inference/ui/pull/1589
- Migration codemod prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/codemods/tree/contrib-hygiene

Risks and trade-offs:
- Additional overhead for small contributions; mitigated by keeping checklists minimal and having a fast-track for tiny, non-API-breaking changes.
- Enforcement vs. guidance balance: prioritize opt-in automation (labeling, action checks) over hard blockers initially.
acceptance_criteria: RFC scaffold template added to Design Confluence and linked in the Contributors README
Onboarding checklist created for tokens, interactive components, and data surfaces (each < 10 checklist items)
Deprecation Signal Registry published with at least 5 actionable signals and two automated issue labels
Maintainers playbook includes a canary + opt-out token plan and a rollback checklist
Two pilot contributions (one token change, one small component update) complete the checklist and provide feedback
proposed_changes: Add RFC template file to /design/rfcs with sections: summary, motivation, compatibility, perf, migration plan, QA checklist, owner, rollout plan
Create three minimal checklists in the repo (tokens.md, components.md, data-surfaces.md) and link them from the PR template
Implement GitHub Action to auto-label PRs based on touched paths and populate 'signal' metadata for future telemetry
Define and document 'deprecation-signal' labels: deprecation-proposed, deprecation-canary, deprecation-final
Ship a small codemod and a migration HOWTO for token renames used during canary phase
